New nonprofit with Piedmont connection

By Christy Guidici · October 7, 2026 · 1 min read

A new Oakland nonprofit, ReQuip, is giving gently used medical equipment and supplies a second life, while making those resources available free of charge to people throughout the community. The organization was created to address two needs at once: improving access to essential medical equipment and keeping usable medical resources out of the landfill.

ReQuip collects, sanitizes and redistributes gently used medical equipment and supplies to individuals who need them. Community members can donate items they no longer need, while people who need equipment for themselves or a family member, are welcome to access the available resources at no cost. It is a place to donate and a resource for anyone who needs these items.

ReQuip accepts a wide range of gently used medical equipment and supplies, including four-wheeled walkers, wheelchairs, continence supplies, bandages, wound care products, braces, shower seats, and other usable medical resources. Information about ReQuip, what can and cannot be accepted, and the mission statement, is available on the website, ReQuipoakland.org. And of course, it would be lovely to have you come volunteer.

The organization was founded on the belief that medical equipment that is no longer of use to one person, can tremendously benefit the next person, while reducing waste, and strengthening community health and independence.

ReQuip will open its doors October 13, and will be open every Tuesday from 10:00 a.m. - 2:00p.m. ReQuip is located in the Oakland Peace Center, 111 Fairmount Avenue at 29th Street. (Look for the blue-wall patio on the right). ReQuipoakland.org
